purpose: Pre-result, falsifiable mechanistic hypotheses about what sets the realized melt-viscosity LEVEL of a resin-modified reactive-PUR candidate inside the 120-130 C processing window. Registered before any Condition-B run and before any Condition-B model call.
decision_question: Is the modified candidate inside the processing-viscosity window at the application temperature?
discriminating_quantity_note: Only a measurement whose resolves_quantity is the realized viscosity level can separate these hypotheses. A thermal-hold drift measurement observes a different coordinate and makes no differential prediction under this registry.
prediction_observable: relative change of the realized viscosity level at matched temperature, percent, against the unmodified reactive-core composition

reference_observations.source: original local unmodified reactive-core realizations at matched temperature
reference_observations.dilution_exponent_basis: declared pre-result power-law exponent relating melt viscosity level to reaction-capable mass fraction in this local family; the exponent is a declared modelling choice, not a fitted local constant
reference_observations.note: Level predictions are expressed relative to the unmodified reactive-core composition of the same lattice, so an unmodified candidate carries no differential prediction and cannot separate these hypotheses.

hypotheses.name: inert-diluent level tracking
hypotheses.statement: Resin-like modifiers are rheologically inert at processing temperature and act only as dilution of reaction-capable material. The realized viscosity level therefore follows a power law in the reactive mass fraction phi_r with no additional modifier-specific contribution.
hypotheses.falsified_if: the measured level differs from the dilution prediction by more than the measurement resolution
hypotheses.supported_if: the measured level agrees with the dilution prediction within the measurement resolution

hypotheses.name: acrylic-associative level elevation
hypotheses.statement: The acrylic-like axis associates within the melt and raises the realized viscosity level above the inert-dilution prediction, in proportion to the acrylic-like loading.
hypotheses.association_gain_basis: declared pre-result elevation rate per percentage point of acrylic-like loading; chosen so the hypothesis makes a separable prediction at the lattice loadings rather than to match any measured outcome
hypotheses.falsified_if: the measured level is at or below the inert-dilution prediction
hypotheses.supported_if: the measured level exceeds the inert-dilution prediction beyond measurement resolution

hypotheses.name: plasticizing-continuum level depression
hypotheses.statement: Both modifier axes act as a plasticizing non-reactive continuum and depress the realized viscosity level below the inert-dilution prediction, in proportion to the total modifier loading.
hypotheses.plasticization_drop_basis: declared pre-result depression rate per percentage point of total modifier loading; chosen so the hypothesis makes a separable prediction at the lattice loadings rather than to match any measured outcome
hypotheses.falsified_if: the measured level is at or above the inert-dilution prediction
hypotheses.supported_if: the measured level falls below the inert-dilution prediction beyond measurement resolution

prediction_floor_basis: a predicted level change below -95% would imply a non-physical near-total loss of melt viscosity and is clipped rather than extrapolated
claim_boundary: These hypotheses are formulation-level statements about the realized viscosity level at matched temperature. None asserts a molecular association mechanism, and none makes any claim about thermal-hold drift, which is the subject of the separate drift registry.
